items.q: Why does Peter Steinberger bet on local-first agents?
items.a: Cloud chatbots do a few things; an agent on your machine can do **everything you can do on the machine** — search files, control devices, surprise you. "If you run on your computer, it can do **every effing thing**."

items.q: What "surprise" moment sold the filesystem thesis?
items.a: The agent found **year-old Sunday audio logs** the user forgot and built a narrative of last year — without explicit setup. Full disk access beats cloud silos.

items.q: Which apps get absorbed by agents?
items.a: Any app that merely **manages data** — fitness tracking, reminders, calorie logs (e.g. MyFitnessPal). Agents that already know context will track, infer, and nudge naturally. "I think **80% of them are going away**."
Apps with **sensors** — cameras, ovens, beds, Tesla hardware. "Only the apps that actually have sensors, maybe they **survive**."

Steinberger favors **swarm/specialist intelligence** — separate bots for work, personal life, relationships — because society specializes, so should agents. Bot-to-bot negotiation (restaurants) may still need a **hired human** for legacy venues.

items.q: How does OpenClaw break vendor memory silos?
items.a: **User-owned markdown memories** on disk — but those files become more sensitive than Google search history. "What's more sensitive — your Google search history or your **memory.md** files?"
**soul.md** / **identity.md** — core values + human-AI interaction norms. Marty infused install templates; one private soul file was **never cracked**.

sections.title: Moats, growth, and contrarian build choices

items.q: Is the model company moat durable?
items.a: Tokens-for-now, but expectations **ratchet every release**; users adapt within a month; open weights from a year ago feel unusable — open source catches up on a ~**1-year lag**.

Couldn't explain on Twitter — a reckless **public Discord demo** (prompt-injection attempts laughed off; owner-only execution) drove understanding. Origin: same ~**9-second** Marrakesh voice improvisation as the TED story.

items.q: What contrarian tooling choices did he make?
items.a: **Codex over Claude Code** (reads more files; ~10 parallel sessions); multiple full repo copies on `main` instead of worktrees; **CLIs over MCP** (Mac Porter converts MCPs to shell on demand) — "Humans don't call MCP manually. They just want to use **CLIs**."
